feed.title: Devin Nunes officially resigns from Congress, clearing way to helm Trump's social media company
feed.summary: Devin Nunes officially resigned from Congress to become CEO of former President Trump's media and technology company, Truth Social. Nunes, a staunch ally of Trump, will lead the new platform which aims to be an alternative to mainstream social media. His move signifies his continued loyalty to Trump and his transition from a congressional career focused initially on local issues to national security and defense of the former president.

feed.title: Smart Water for a Smarter Home: Moen Leads the Way with Industry's First Whole-Home Connected Water Product Suite
feed.summary: Moen introduces the industry's first whole-home smart water ecosystem, the Moen Smart Water Network, which allows consumers to control, monitor, and conserve water throughout their homes using a single smartphone app. The network includes new and expanded smart products like the Flo Smart Water Monitor and Shutoff, Smart Leak Detector, Smart Sump Pump Monitor, Smart Faucet with Motion Control, and Smart Shower, all designed to provide peace of mind, security, and personalized water experiences. These innovations offer automated water security, water usage education, personalized settings, and voice activation capabilities for a truly connected home water system.

feed.title: Apple becomes first company to hit $3 trillion market value, then slips
feed.summary: Apple Inc. briefly touched a $3 trillion stock market valuation on January 3, 2022, becoming the first company to reach this milestone, fueled by investor confidence in its product pipeline and expansion into new markets like automated cars and virtual reality. Although its market capitalization slipped just below $3 trillion by day's end, the achievement highlights the company's strong fundamentals and consumer loyalty for its iPhones, MacBooks, and services. The stock has seen significant growth since the first iPhone launch in 2007, and under CEO Tim Cook, Apple has successfully diversified its revenue streams beyond the iPhone.

feed.title: Investor Michael Seibel Explains Google’s Search Quality Decline And How It’s Creating Opportunities
feed.summary: Investor Michael Seibel, a partner and CEO at Y Combinator, has voiced concerns about the declining quality of Google Search results, particularly in categories like health, product reviews, and recipes, attributing the problem to Google's focus on short-term ad revenue. He believes this opens opportunities for disruptive startups, despite Google's dominant market share. Seibel highlighted that while DuckDuckGo offers an alternative, the fundamental issue lies in Google prioritizing monetization over user search experience.

feed.title: 3 BYOD security risks and how to prevent them
feed.summary: The increasing adoption of Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) policies introduces significant security challenges for organizations, despite offering cost savings and flexibility. Key risks include data theft stemming from personal logins and cloud synchronization, unclear security protocols leading to shadow IT and employee-driven breaches, and the prevalence of mobile malware. Effective prevention requires robust mobile device management policies, including encryption, application blacklisting, regular data backups, and thorough employee security training.

feed.title: Qualcomm inks car chip deals with Volvo, Honda and Renault
feed.summary: Qualcomm announced deals to supply chips to automakers Volvo Group, Honda Motor Co Ltd, and Renault SA, accelerating its push into the automotive sector. The company will provide its "Snapdragon Cockpit" chips for digital dashboards and infotainment systems, aiming to help car manufacturers transform vehicles into rolling computers capable of over-the-air updates and generating recurring revenue. Qualcomm also unveiled a new chip and system, "Snapdragon Ride Vision System," for computer vision and safety features, utilizing technology from its recent acquisition of Arriver.

feed.title: $20 Billion In 2022: Google Pays Apple For Not Launching Its Own Search Engine?
feed.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Apple and Google, alleging an illegal agreement where Google pays Apple billions annually to remain the default search engine on Apple devices and prevents Apple from developing its own search engine. The lawsuit claims this arrangement violates US antitrust law, stifles competition, and inflates advertising rates. While both companies have been discreet about the exact figures, estimates suggest Google could pay Apple around $20 billion in 2022, accounting for a significant portion of Apple's annual earnings.

feed.title: Iberdrola optimizes working capital with SAP® Real-Time Treasury
feed.summary: Iberdrola, a global leader in renewable energy, has partnered with J.P. Morgan to implement the SAP® Real-Time Treasury app. This integration provides Iberdrola with real-time visibility into their global cash positions, streamlines treasury operations, and enhances their ability to respond to market changes. The solution, powered by J.P. Morgan's Treasury Services APIs, has migrated Iberdrola from daily reporting to instant access to financial data, optimizing their working capital management.

feed.title: Google users fume as smart speaker features disappear following Sonos patent ruling
feed.summary: Following a ruling by the United States International Trade Commission that Google violated five Sonos patents, Google has removed certain smart speaker features, specifically related to group volume control. Nest smart speaker users are frustrated by these changes, which now require individual volume adjustments for speakers in a group. Google is facing a potential import ban on products infringing on Sonos's patents, while Sonos suggests Google could pay royalties.

feed.title: JVAL Stock Price | JPMorgan U.S. Value Factor ETF
feed.summary: This article provides detailed information about the JPMorgan U.S. Value Factor ETF (JVAL), including its current stock price, trading exchange (NYSE), and comprehensive financial metrics such as dividend yield, expense ratio, and market capitalization. It also offers technical analysis insights and lists the ETF's top holdings, outlining its investment strategy as a value-focused equity fund targeting the U.S. market.

feed.title: BlackBerry smartphones: what impact did they have on the workplace?
feed.summary: BlackBerry discontinued services for its legacy devices, marking the end of an era for a device that significantly impacted the workplace. While BlackBerrys enabled remote work and efficiency, they also blurred work-life boundaries, a challenge still faced today. HR professionals reflect on the devices' dual impact, from increased productivity to the expectation of constant availability.

feed.title: Google loses Sonos smart speakers patent fight
feed.summary: Smart-speaker firm Sonos has won a major legal battle against Google, with the US International Trade Commission ruling that Google infringed on five of Sonos' patents related to multi-room audio technology. This decision could lead to a ban on importing infringing Google smart home tech into the United States, and Sonos suggests Google may have to "degrade" its products or pay licensing fees. Google disputes the ruling, stating it has already developed workarounds and does not expect the decision to impact its ability to sell products.

feed.title: Santa Barbara-Based Company Wins Legal Battle Against Google Over Patent
feed.summary: Santa Barbara-based company Sonos won a legal battle against Google, with the U.S. International Trade Commission ruling that Google infringed on five Sonos patents related to smart speaker technology. This ruling includes a cease-and-desist order and an import ban on infringing Google products, specifically concerning Google's Nest speakers and their volume adjustment capabilities. Sonos has two additional patent-infringement cases against Google pending in federal courts.

feed.title: Apple Could Reinvent Money Management, Take on PayPal and Robinhood
feed.summary: Apple has the potential to significantly disrupt the financial technology (fintech) sector by expanding its Apple Card offerings, introducing checking accounts, and developing new money management tools. This strategic move could position Apple as a direct competitor to established players like PayPal and Robinhood. The author suggests Apple is poised for a major impact in this space, with further developments expected in 2022.

feed.title: Updating My Favorite Performance Chart For 2021
feed.summary: Ben Carlson updates his asset allocation quilt for 2021, analyzing the performance of various asset classes over the last decade. He highlights REITs' surprising strong performance, the ongoing struggles of commodities despite recent gains, and the consistent outperformance of the S&P 500. The article also discusses the impact of diversification and the impressive long-term returns of U.S. stocks even when including the 2008 financial crisis.

feed.title: Akron Marathon registration details, sponsorships announced
feed.summary: Registration for the 20th Akron Marathon Race Series opens on January 20, with early registration for eligible participants starting on January 18. Key sponsors FirstEnergy Corp., Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co., and National Interstate Insurance Co. have renewed their support through 2024. The article outlines the dates and locations for the various races, including the National Interstate 8K and 1 Mile, Goodyear Half Marathon and 10K, and the FirstEnergy Akron Marathon, Half Marathon, and team relay.

feed.title: PacBio and Google Collaborate to Use Machine Learning to Optimize Long-Read Sequencing Data Analysis
feed.summary: PacBio announced a research collaboration with Google to use machine learning to optimize long-read sequencing data analysis. This collaboration aims to improve PacBio's HiFi sequencing accuracy and data output by integrating Google's genomic analysis, machine learning, and algorithm development tools. The partnership is expected to further enhance variant calling and unlock more insights from PacBio sequencing data for various applications.

feed.title: Welcoming the Post-Zoom Era
feed.summary: The article discusses the impending end of the "Zoom era," noting a waning enthusiasm for constant video conferencing, even among those previously reliant on it. Author Jonathan Bartlett observes that people are increasingly opting out of Zoom meetings and classes, highlighting the draining nature of online interaction compared to in-person engagement. He suggests that organizations must soon decide whether to be primarily remote or in-person, and for remote setups, managers will need to minimize Zoom time and find alternative ways to foster team cohesion to prevent a decline in loyalty.

feed.title: J.B. Hunt, Waymo expand partnership on self-driving truck technology
feed.summary: J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc. and Waymo Via are expanding their strategic alliance to integrate commercial autonomous driving technology into transportation and logistics, aiming for fully autonomous transport in Texas within the next few years. This long-term partnership builds on a successful 2021 pilot and will include multiple trials to analyze the operational capacity of Waymo Via's autonomous Class 8 trucking unit. The collaboration also seeks to merge autonomous driving technology with J.B. Hunt’s digital freight marketplace and refine the technology's commercial readiness.

feed.title: Here’s How Warren Buffett Persuaded Google’s Reluctant Founders to Go Public
feed.summary: Google co-founders Sergey Brin and Larry Page were initially hesitant to take their company public due to fears of losing control. A serendipitous meeting with Warren Buffett, who shared his strategy of a two-tier stock structure used at Berkshire Hathaway, convinced them that they could go public while retaining control. This led Google to adopt a similar stock structure for its IPO and publish an "Owner's Manual" outlining their long-term philosophy for shareholders.

feed.title: A Full List Of Uber Subsidiaries [& How They Benefit Uber]
feed.summary: This article details Uber's various subsidiaries, including Uber Eats, Uber Freight, and UberWAV, alongside its corporate structure and key leadership. It also outlines significant acquisitions such as Jump Bikes, Careem, Drizly, and Postmates, and discusses previously owned entities like Raiser LLC and Xchange Leasing. The piece highlights Uber's expansion into a global transportation and e-commerce giant, aiming for a future with driver-less transportation.

feed.title: D-Wave increases European presence with quantum computer in Germany
feed.summary: D-Wave Systems Inc. has expanded its European presence by providing an annealing quantum computer to the Forschungszentrum Jülich Supercomputing Centre in Germany, claiming it's the first such device in Europe. This move is part of D-Wave's strategy to accelerate commercialization in the growing quantum computing market, despite facing significant competition from tech giants and other quantum startups. The company, a long-standing Canadian firm, aims to leverage its new association with Germany to capture a larger share of the market for solving complex optimization problems.

feed.title: Chip giant Nvidia expands R&D operations in Israel
feed.summary: Nvidia is expanding its R&D operations in Israel by establishing a new design and engineering group focused on next-generation CPUs for AI, robotics, and autonomous vehicles. The company, which acquired Israel's Mellanox Technologies in 2020, plans to hire additional engineers in Israel, further solidifying the country's role as Nvidia's largest R&D hub outside the US. This expansion intensifies competition for tech talent in Israel, where both Nvidia and Intel have significant R&D presence, and Google is also entering the chip-making sector.

feed.title: Oracle opens data centre to provide cloud services across Africa
feed.summary: Oracle has launched its first data center in South Africa, providing local cloud services across the African continent to better compete with rivals like Microsoft and Amazon. The new data center in Johannesburg is Oracle's 37th "cloud region" globally, with plans to reach 44 this year. This move caters to the increasing demand for faster computing from African banks and telecom firms, despite challenges such as high power prices and frequent outages in South Africa.

feed.title: Employee surveillance is exploding with remote work—and could be the new norm
feed.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated the adoption of employee surveillance software, with 60% of large companies using these technologies by the end of 2021, compared to 30% pre-pandemic. This expansion of monitoring into employees' homes raises significant concerns about privacy, trust, and the blurring of work-life boundaries. Experts warn of "function creep," where temporary surveillance measures become permanent, and highlight the urgent need for new legal protections for workers' privacy, as existing laws are largely weak and inadequate for the evolving landscape of remote work.

feed.title: How to Invest in the Top 100 U.S. ESG Companies
feed.summary: The article discusses the 2022 list of top 100 U.S. ESG companies compiled by Just Capital, highlighting major movements like Alphabet's rise and Meta's fall. It explains the methodology behind the rankings, which prioritize issues important to Americans, and introduces the Goldman Sachs JUST U.S. Large Cap Equity ETF (JUST) as a way to invest in companies demonstrating "just business behavior."

feed.title: Certification programs build digital skills
feed.summary: The Economic Development Corporation Michigan City (EDCMC) and Goodwill Industries of Michiana are collaborating to offer certification programs for digital skill enhancement. These online courses, including Facebook Social Media Marketing and Google IT Support, aim to help community members earn stackable certificates in high-demand fields. The programs are designed to assist individuals in overcoming barriers to education and employment by providing coursework, mentorship, and job placement services.

feed.title: What is HPC-as-a-service and why does it matter?
feed.summary: High Performance Compute-as-a-service (HPCaaS) is emerging as a critical cloud service, offering hardware, software, and expertise to process demanding workloads like big data analytics. This service addresses the challenges companies face with in-house HPC, such as high costs and specialized staffing, by leveraging cloud infrastructure from providers like IBM and Microsoft Azure. While offering benefits like faster technology integration and dynamic management, HPCaaS also presents challenges related to security, licensing costs, and data transfer, though experts believe these will be overcome by continued innovation, with the market projected to reach $17 billion by 2026.

feed.title: Microsoft secures IPs like Call of Duty and Candy Crash to boost its metaverse ambitions, analyst says
feed.summary: Microsoft's $68.7 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard is seen as a strategic move to bolster its metaverse ambitions, according to analyst Joost Rietveld. The deal secures popular gaming franchises like Call of Duty and Candy Crush, potentially differentiating Microsoft's Game Pass service and influencing cross-platform availability. While Microsoft has committed to honoring existing agreements, allowing Call of Duty to remain on PlayStation for now, the long-term impact on platform exclusivity for other IPs remains uncertain.

feed.title: SRE: Benefits and Business Impact of the SRE Mindset
feed.summary: This article discusses the benefits and business impact of adopting a Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) mindset. It explains how SRE, originating from Google, offers a concrete model to implement the DevOps philosophy by balancing feature development velocity with operational reliability risks. The SRE model aims to raise operational excellence, foster unified engineering vision, and redefine operations as a value creation center through concepts like SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets.

feed.title: Strategas Macro Thematic Opportunities ETF
feed.summary: This page provides a detailed profile of the Strategas Macro Thematic Opportunities ETF (SAMT), including its current price, dividend information, expense ratio, holdings, and performance data. It also offers comparisons to other ETFs in its category and segment, along with ESG themes and scores. The ETF launched on January 26, 2022, and is actively managed by Baird Financial Group Inc.

feed.title: Intel scores major win as court scraps $1.2 bln EU antitrust fine
feed.summary: Intel has successfully overturned a 1.06-billion-euro ($1.2 billion) EU antitrust fine that was imposed 12 years ago for allegedly stifling rival Advanced Micro Devices. Europe's second-highest court annulled the fine, criticizing the European Commission's analysis as incomplete. This ruling is a significant setback for EU antitrust regulators and could impact similar cases involving other major tech companies.

feed.title: 11 Undervalued Mega-Cap Stocks to Consider
feed.summary: This article identifies 11 undervalued mega-cap stocks that investors should consider, defining mega-caps as companies with market capitalizations over $200 billion. It highlights that the recent market downturn has brought many such stocks into buying range, including detailed analysis for Alphabet, Amazon.com, and AT&T.

feed.title: Neil Young’s dispute with Spotify over Joe Rogan increases pressure on streamer to monitor content
feed.summary: Neil Young's dispute with Spotify over vaccine misinformation on Joe Rogan's podcast has put the streaming giant under significant pressure to monitor its content more closely. Spotify, which removed Young's music but kept Rogan's podcast, announced it would add content advisories to all COVID-19 related podcast episodes. This incident highlights the challenges platforms face in balancing free speech with preventing the spread of misinformation, especially given Spotify's substantial investments in podcasts for business growth.

feed.title: Adobe XD Review
feed.summary: Adobe XD is a powerful and intuitive design software for interactive interface design and prototyping, recognized as an Editors' Choice. It excels due to its seamless integration with other Creative Cloud apps and robust responsive design tools. While Sketch is Mac-only, Adobe XD supports both macOS and Windows, making it a versatile option for UI/UX designers, despite having fewer plug-ins than its competitor.

feed.title: Google (GOOGL) announces 20-for-1 stock split
feed.summary: Google's parent company Alphabet announced a 20-for-1 stock split proposal, aiming to make Google stock more affordable and abundant for investors. This news followed an impressive Q4 2021 earnings report where Google beat Wall Street expectations, driven by investments in AI and strong Pixel phone sales. If approved, existing shareholders by July 1, 2022, will receive 19 additional shares for each original share by July 15.

feed.title: Google parent Alphabet announces 20-for-1 stock split
feed.summary: Alphabet, Google's parent company, announced a 20-for-1 stock split following a surge in its stock price. This move aims to make shares more accessible to a wider range of investors by significantly lowering the per-share cost. The split requires shareholder approval and will involve Class A, B, and C shares, with existing holders receiving 19 additional shares for each one they own by July 15.

feed.title: Income Is The Outcome
feed.summary: The article discusses the JPMorgan Equity Premium Income Fund, an income-oriented fund that uses equity-linked notes (ELNs) and options premiums to generate substantial income for investors. Despite underperforming market benchmarks in total return, its strategy prioritizes income generation and aims to reduce volatility, allowing investors to stay invested in equities in a more defensive manner. The fund's co-portfolio manager, Hamilton Reiner, explains how the use of ELNs converts options premiums into bona fide income and how market volatility influences the income generated.

feed.title: Univision, Televisa Complete $4.8B Merger
feed.summary: Grupo Televisa, S.A.B and Univision Holdings II, Inc. have completed their $4.8 billion merger, creating TelevisaUnivision, Inc., a new company poised to reach over 100 million Spanish-language speakers daily across TV, digital, and audio. The newly formed entity plans to launch a major streaming service in 2022, featuring free and premium tiers with a vast offering of original Spanish-language entertainment, sports, and news. New investors in TelevisaUnivision include SoftBank Latin America Fund, Google, and The Raine Group.

feed.title: Google's parent company Alphabet announces 20-for-1 stock split
feed.summary: Alphabet, Google's parent company, announced a 20-for-1 stock split during its quarterly earnings report, aiming to make shares more accessible. The split, which applies to all share classes (A, B, and C), is pending shareholder approval and would take effect in July 2022. This move follows a significant doubling of Alphabet's stock value in the preceding two years, with each share potentially revalued to $137.64 from $2,752.88 after the split.

feed.title: Google parent Alphabet is splitting its stock 20-for-1. Here's why, and what it means for investors.
feed.summary: Alphabet announced a 20-for-1 stock split to make its shares more affordable and appealing to smaller investors, with Class A shares potentially dropping to around $138 from over $2,750. This move could also facilitate its entry into the Dow Jones Industrial Average, although the company's fundamentals and market capitalization will remain unchanged. All shareholders will receive 19 additional shares of the same class as a dividend on July 15 if the plan is approved.

feed.title: Google (Alphabet) Q4 2021 Earnings Report Recap
feed.summary: Alphabet Inc. (Google) reported better-than-expected Q4 FY 2021 earnings and revenue, driven by strong advertiser spending, increased consumer online activity, and growth in Google Cloud. Despite higher-than-anticipated traffic acquisition costs, the company's shares rose, and its board approved a 20-for-one stock split, pending shareholder approval. CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted a significant increase in the cloud business backlog and growth in cloud deals over $1 billion.

feed.title: Alphabet Stock Split: A Win for Retail Investors … And the Dow?
feed.summary: Alphabet's 20-for-1 stock split aims to make its shares more accessible to retail investors and potentially opens the door for its inclusion in the Dow Jones Industrial Average. While fundamentally inconsequential, the split could provide a tailwind for GOOGL stock. Its impact on the Dow would also be significant, altering sector weighting and index composition considerations.

feed.title: Alphabet brings big stock splits back to market
authors: Jeran Wittenstein and Vivianne Rodrigues and Bloomberg
feed.summary: Alphabet Inc. announced a 20-for-1 stock split, aiming to make its shares more accessible to small investors by reducing the per-share price. This move is also seen as a step towards potential inclusion in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which has historically been a barrier due to Alphabet's high stock price. The announcement led to a 10% jump in shares during premarket trading.

feed.title: NICE Expands Partnership with Google, Adding CXone to the Chrome Enterprise Recommended Program
feed.summary: NICE has expanded its partnership with Google, integrating its CXone customer experience platform into the Chrome Enterprise Recommended program. This optimization allows organizations using Chrome OS devices to leverage CXone's comprehensive suite of CX applications for efficient work-from-anywhere capabilities, enhancing both agent and customer experiences. The move reinforces NICE's commitment to providing next-gen, digitally fluent experiences on Chrome OS, supporting millions of interactions for various businesses.

feed.title: Alphabet eyes $2 trillion value after blowout results
feed.summary: Alphabet Inc. is on the verge of joining Apple and Microsoft in the $2 trillion market valuation club after a strong quarterly report led to an over 8% surge in its shares. The company also announced a 20-to-1 stock split, aiming to make shares more accessible to retail investors. At least 20 brokerages raised their price targets on Alphabet's stock.

feed.title: Alphabet Stock Is Splitting. Why It Still Matters in the Age of Fractional Shares.
feed.summary: Alphabet, Google's parent company, announced a 20-for-1 stock split alongside a robust fourth-quarter 2021 earnings report. The article discusses why this stock split is still relevant, even with the increasing availability of fractional shares.

feed.title: 10 immutable laws of security administration redux
feed.summary: This article revisits Scott Culp's "10 Immutable Laws of Security Administration" 20 years after their initial publication. The author, Brett James, analyzes each law to assess its continued relevance in today's cybersecurity landscape. He concludes that most of the laws remain highly applicable, with some requiring updated technological contexts, and highlights the ongoing importance of vigilance, good administration, and risk management in security.

feed.title: Google Cloud Announces Cloud-First Partnership with KeyBank
feed.summary: Google Cloud, KeyBank, and Deloitte have announced an expanded, multi-year strategic partnership to accelerate KeyBank's cloud-first approach to banking. KeyBank will become one of the largest regional banks to operate its primary platforms and applications on Google Cloud, leveraging AI and data solutions to deliver enhanced digital experiences. Deloitte will facilitate the migration of KeyBank's infrastructure to Google Cloud, with the goal of moving the majority of its products and services to the cloud by 2025.

feed.title: Amazon notches up sunny sales, despite client shift to 'multicloud',
feed.summary: Amazon's cloud computing division, Amazon Web Services (AWS), has continued to show strong sales growth for four consecutive quarters, easing concerns that a move towards "multicloud" strategies by clients would diminish its market share. While some companies are adopting multiple cloud vendors for diversification, major players like AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud are still gaining market share from smaller competitors, indicating that even in a multicloud approach, a primary cloud provider often remains dominant. This robust performance underscores significant growth in the wider cloud industry, with overall spending jumping by 37% in 2021.

feed.title: KeyBank taps Google Cloud and Deloitte to become cloud-first lender
feed.summary: KeyBank has partnered with Google Cloud and Deloitte to transition its banking operations to a cloud-first model by 2025. This multi-year collaboration aims to migrate primary platforms and applications to Google Cloud infrastructure, using its data solutions and AI technologies to enhance personalised digital banking experiences and secure client services. Deloitte will serve as the systems integrator for this migration.

feed.title: News Corp’s deal with Google and the Melbourne Business School questioned by journalism academics
feed.summary: Journalism academics are questioning the newly announced Digital News Academy, a partnership between News Corp Australia, Google, and the Melbourne Business School. Critics argue that housing the academy within a business school rather than a journalism program undermines academic rigor and independent criticism, especially given News Corp's historical animosity towards university journalism education and its reliance on Google funding. The academics emphasize the importance of distinguishing between skills training and comprehensive education that includes ethics and critical thinking within the industry.

feed.title: Opinion: $1.4 trillion? Big Tech’s pandemic year produces mind-boggling financial results
feed.summary: In 2021, despite supply-chain disruptions, labor shortages, and rising prices, major tech companies including Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, and Microsoft achieved staggering financial results. They collectively saw over $320 billion in profit on $1.4 trillion in sales, with profits increasing more than 55% and sales growing 27% from an already record-setting base. This performance highlights Big Tech's resilience and expanding economic influence, making their combined sales comparable to a top-15 global economy.

feed.title: Amazon hiking base salary cap to $350,000 for corporate, tech workers
feed.summary: Amazon has announced a significant increase in its base salary cap for corporate and tech workers, raising it from $160,000 to $350,000. This move aims to enhance the company's competitiveness in a challenging labor market and attract and retain top talent. The company indicated that these increases are "much more considerable" than in previous years, aligning its pay structure more closely with other major tech firms.

feed.title: Nvidia’s $40bn takeover of UK chip designer Arm collapses
feed.summary: Nvidia's $40bn takeover of UK chip designer Arm has collapsed due to insurmountable regulatory hurdles, leading Arm to pursue a stock market flotation instead. The deal, which had been valued as high as $75bn, faced fierce opposition and regulatory scrutiny in multiple regions, including the US, UK, and China. Softbank will now prepare Arm for an IPO and receive a $1.25bn break-up fee from Nvidia.

feed.title: Want Exposure To Google? 2 Communication Services ETFs Holding Alphabet Shares
feed.summary: This article discusses two Communication Services ETFs, the Fidelity MSCI Telecommunication Services Index ETF (FCOM) and the iShares Global Comm Services ETF (IXP), that offer significant exposure to Alphabet shares. It highlights Alphabet's strong Q4 and FY 2021 results, including a 20-for-1 stock split, and reviews the holdings, performance, and key metrics of each ETF for investors looking to capitalize on the growth in this sector.

feed.title: Anger after News Corp and Google Australia set up journalism academy at university business school
feed.summary: News Corp Australia and Google Australia have partnered to establish the Digital News Academy, offering a nine-month journalism course through the University of Melbourne's business school. This initiative has sparked controversy among academics at the university, who express anger and concern over not being consulted and the choice of the business school over traditional journalism programs. Critics view this move as a reflection of News Corp's historical antagonism towards university journalism and question the focus on "commercial journalism."

feed.title: PEPSI® Develops New Platform with Verizon to Immerse Fans into Pepsi Super Bowl Halftime Show with Live 360-degree Mobile Experience
feed.summary: Pepsi and Verizon have partnered to launch the "Pepsi Super Bowl Halftime Show ULTRA PASS Powered by Verizon 5G Ultra Wideband," an immersive mobile experience for Super Bowl LVI. This platform will provide fans with live 360-degree on-field and on-stage access to the halftime show through a dedicated app, utilizing Verizon's 5G technology. The initiative aims to enhance the broadcast viewing experience by offering exclusive vantage points and bringing fans closer to the performers.

feed.title: Corporate lobbying ETF seeks to profit from influencing politicians
feed.summary: Strategas Asset Management has launched a new exchange-traded fund (ETF), the Strategas Global Policy Opportunities ETF (SAGP-A), designed to invest in companies that demonstrate a strong return on their lobbying efforts in the U.S. federal government. The ETF aims to capitalize on corporate lobbying as a means for companies to gain an earnings advantage, especially in a politically volatile environment. While the existing portfolio has underperformed in recent years, the new ETF includes small and mid-cap companies and non-U.S. firms, which are believed to achieve better returns on lobbying spend, despite some ethical concerns raised by analysts.

feed.title: Is Qualcomm’s New ‘aptX Lossless’ Technology The Holy Grail of Bluetooth?
feed.summary: Qualcomm has announced 'aptX Lossless,' a new capability within its aptX Adaptive codec, designed to deliver true CD-quality (16-bit, 44.1kHz) lossless audio over Bluetooth. This technology aims to overcome the traditional lossy compression of Bluetooth by optimizing wireless connectivity and audio technologies to scale up to approximately 1Mbps for lossless transfer. This development could be a significant step for audiophiles and addresses the growing consumer demand for higher quality streaming audio, allowing the clear transmission of lossless source content from services like Amazon HD.

feed.title: Telkom Kembali Jadi Satu-satunya Perusahaan Indonesia yang Masuk Jajaran Brand Finance Global 500
feed.summary: Telkom Indonesia has once again been recognized as the only Indonesian company to be included in the Brand Finance Global 500 Most Valuable Brand list for 2022, marking its fifth entry. With a brand value of US$4.69 billion, Telkom ranked 490, ahead of many international brands, highlighting the success of its digital transformation strategy. The company also received the award for Indonesia's Most Valuable Brand 2021, credited to its strong brand rating and robust financial performance in Q3 2021.

feed.title: YouTube floats ideas of verifying NFTs, watching games in metaverse
feed.summary: YouTube is exploring using blockchain technology and NFTs to help creators find new ways to monetize content by offering verifiable digital assets. The company also suggested ideas for the metaverse, focusing on enhancing social viewing experiences, particularly for gaming content, to allow users to watch videos together in a virtual environment. These initiatives aim to cut down on fraud in the digital art market and improve user engagement.

feed.title: Can A Vintage T. Rowe Price Fund Ride Rivian, Microsoft And Snap To The Moon?
feed.summary: Portfolio manager Joe Fath is revitalizing the T. Rowe Price Growth Stock Fund, founded in 1950, by investing heavily in new tech companies and focusing on "disruptive change," contrasting with the fund's historical picks like IBM. Despite facing outflows to passive management, Fath's strategy involves concentrated bets in private companies like Rivian, and public tech giants such as Microsoft, achieving significant returns. He remains confident in these high-growth, high-volatility investments, believing their long-term growth profiles will ultimately reward shareholders.

feed.title: Best Load Balancers & Load Balancing Software
feed.summary: This article reviews the best load balancers and load balancing software solutions available, covering a range of types including hardware, software, cloud, and virtual appliances. It details offerings from major vendors like A10 Networks, AWS, Citrix, F5, HAProxy, and VMware, comparing their features, pros, and cons. The piece also explains what load balancing is, how it works, different load balancing algorithms, and what application delivery controllers (ADCs) are, helping readers choose the right solution for their IT infrastructure.

feed.title: Jobs in Hyderabad: Microsoft invites applications from freshers
feed.summary: Microsoft is inviting applications from freshers for engineering jobs in its Hyderabad office. Eligible candidates must have a B.Tech, M.Tech, or MS degree in Computer Science or a related field with a minimum CGPA of 7.5/10 and be from the 2022 batch. Selected candidates may work in Hyderabad, Bangalore, or Noida, with responsibilities including planning, design, and implementation.

feed.title: Harry Potter: Magic Awakened is coming to mobile devices
feed.summary: Warner Bros. Games and NetEase have announced that "Harry Potter: Magic Awakened," a free-to-play collectible card and massive multiplayer duelling game with RPG elements, is launching in the Americas, Europe, and Oceania. Players can pre-register now on Google Play for the game, which allows them to experience life as a Hogwarts student, customize characters, learn spells, and duel other players. The game features characters from the original series alongside new faces and a robust multiplayer experience.

feed.title: Dutch judges deny Google injunction request against Sonos
feed.summary: A Dutch court has rejected Google's request for an injunction against Sonos regarding an alleged patent infringement related to smart speaker technology. Google sought to prevent Sonos from infringing on its "Domain-based digital-rights management system with easy and secure device enrollment" patent (EP 621) in the UK, Italy, or Finland, and also requested Sonos inform customers of the alleged infringement. The court dismissed Google's claim, stating a lack of specification in the writ of summons, found that Sonos did not infringe the patent, and ordered Google to pay costs of €200,000 to Sonos.

feed.title: Vodafone Idea (Vi) Promoters Disappointing Investors
feed.summary: Vodafone Idea's promoters, including Aditya Birla Group and Vodafone Group Plc, have failed to inject much-needed capital into the company, causing it to struggle financially. This lack of investment is detrimental to Vi's ability to compete in upcoming 5G spectrum auctions and expand its network, potentially leading to increased subscriber churn. Despite government assistance, the promoters have shown no initiative, leading to a lack of confidence from outside investors.

feed.title: Copyright case: Google LLC v. Oracle America Inc., USA
authors: Thomas Long (Wolters Kluwer Legal & Regulatory US)
feed.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in favor of Google LLC in a significant copyright case against Oracle America, Inc. The Court determined that Google's use of approximately 11,000 lines of code from Java SE API for its Android mobile operating system constituted fair use and did not infringe on Oracle's copyright. This decision, dubbed "the copyright case of the decade" by Google, was a six-to-two ruling.

feed.title: Sonos IKEA Symfonisk Table Lamp Speaker with WiFi (Gen 2) review
feed.summary: The Sonos IKEA Symfonisk Table Lamp Speaker with WiFi (Gen 2) is a stylish second-generation lamp speaker offering improved audio and a modular design with interchangeable shades. While it delivers solid trebles and mid-range sounds comparable to other Sonos devices, bass performance can suffer at high volumes. Despite being a little pricey and lacking built-in smart assistant functions, its elegant design and multi-room audio capabilities make it a practical choice for Apple users seeking a discrete speaker solution.

feed.title: Billionaire George Soros reveals stake in Rivian, sells some tech shares
feed.summary: Billionaire George Soros' investment fund, Soros Fund Management, acquired a significant stake in electric-pickup maker Rivian Automotive Inc., purchasing nearly 20 million shares worth approximately $2 billion in Q4. This move was disclosed in a recent SEC filing. At the same time, Soros' fund also trimmed positions in major tech companies like Amazon and Alphabet.

feed.title: Stanley Druckenmiller Buys Chevron as Family Offices Reveal Stock Picks
feed.summary: Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office sold its Meta Platforms Inc. position and bought Chevron, indicating a shift away from big tech. Similarly, George Soros's family office reduced its stakes in Amazon.com, Alphabet, and a Nasdaq 100 ETF. These moves suggest a trend among some wealthy investors to re-evaluate their portfolios regarding large technology companies.

feed.title: John Deere and Brazilian bank team up to equip farmers deforesting the Amazon
feed.summary: An investigation has revealed that farmers in Brazil, some with properties embargoed by environmental authorities for Amazon deforestation and outstanding environmental fines, have been accessing government-subsidized loans to purchase John Deere tractors. These loans are administered by the state-owned Brazilian Development Bank (BNDES) and underwritten by John Deere Bank, a subsidiary of the U.S. manufacturer. This practice highlights a loophole in Central Bank rules intended to bar such credit, raising concerns about the misuse of public funds and the enforcement of environmental regulations in Brazil.

feed.title: Tesla Stock vs. Alphabet Stock: Which Is the Better Buy Today?
feed.summary: Morningstar compares Tesla (TSLA) and Alphabet (GOOGL) stock using proprietary metrics to determine which is the better investment. Alphabet is found to be undervalued and has a wider economic moat and lower uncertainty compared to Tesla, which is currently overvalued. Based on their ratings, Morningstar identifies Alphabet as the overall better buy today.

feed.title: India Bans 54 Chinese Apps Including That From Sea, Alibaba, NetEase, Tencent
feed.summary: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has banned 54 apps identified as being of Chinese origin, including Sea Ltd.'s popular game Free Fire, as well as apps from Tencent Holdings Ltd, Alibaba Group Holding Ltd, and NetEase Inc. This ban targets re-branded versions of applications previously prohibited in 2020 and stems from ongoing geopolitical tensions between India and China, particularly following a 2020 skirmish. Free Fire, a battle royale shooter, was notably India's highest-grossing mobile game in Q3 before the ban.

feed.title: Akamai pays $900M to acquire AWS cloud infrastructure rival Linode
feed.summary: Akamai Technologies Inc. has announced its acquisition of Linode LLC for approximately $900 million. This strategic move aims to transform Akamai into a highly distributed compute platform, enhancing its offerings for developers by combining Linode's cloud computing capabilities with Akamai's edge platform and security tools. The acquisition follows Akamai's strong fourth-quarter financial results and is expected to add about $100 million in revenue by year-end.

feed.title: Why Trump’s TRUTH Social Platform Will Struggle to Compete With Mainstream Social Media
feed.summary: Experts predict that Donald Trump's TRUTH Social platform will struggle to compete with mainstream social media despite its appeal to conservative users. The platform's inherently ideological focus and lack of broad social features are expected to limit its growth potential, as previous right-wing alternatives have similarly failed to achieve large-scale success. While Trump's personal influence might initially draw users, the long-term viability is questioned due to the platform's niche focus and lack of technological innovation.

feed.title: JPMorgan Chase spent $2 billion on brand new data centers last year
feed.summary: JPMorgan Chase invested $2 billion in new data centers last year, even while actively migrating data and applications to public cloud platforms like AWS, Google, and Microsoft. This investment is part of their broader annual technology spending, which exceeded $12 billion, focusing on cloud capabilities, digital consumer experience, and data analytics. CEO Jamie Dimon emphasized that the new data centers incorporate "cloud capability," and the firm plans to move 30% to 50% of its applications to the cloud this year, driven by the significant value seen in risk management, fraud prevention, and customer satisfaction.

feed.title: Waymo partners with logistics giant to run self-driving trucks between Dallas and Houston
feed.summary: Waymo, Alphabet Inc.'s self-driving technology unit, has partnered with logistics giant C.H. Robinson to pilot autonomous freight hauling between Dallas and Houston on Interstate 45. These self-driving trucks, which will include a safety driver, aim to address long-term driver shortages and improve the carrier and driver experience. Waymo has established a 9-acre hub in South Dallas for its autonomous trucking operations, leveraging Texas's status as a major freight hub.

feed.title: Jaguar Land Rover, Nvidia ally in vehicle software arms race
feed.summary: Luxury automaker Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has partnered with Nvidia to develop advanced computer brains and software for its vehicles launching from 2025 onwards. This collaboration aims to accelerate JLR's in-vehicle software development, enabling features like autonomous driving and parking, and providing more digital functions to drivers. The deal is a significant win for Nvidia in expanding its automotive industry presence and helps JLR compete with rivals like Tesla in digital technology.

feed.title: C.H. Robinson to Test Self-Driving Trucks with Waymo
feed.summary: C.H. Robinson is partnering with Waymo Via to test self-driving trucks, aiming to address the ongoing trucker shortage and improve efficiency in logistics. The collaboration will involve Waymo Via's autonomous trucks carrying C.H. Robinson freight between Dallas and Houston, utilizing C.H. Robinson's extensive shipping lane data to optimize routes. This long-term strategic partnership leverages Waymo's established autonomous vehicle technology for road safety and operational efficiency.

feed.title: Charlie Munger Calls US-China Tensions `Massively Stupid’
feed.summary: Charlie Munger, Warren Buffett's longtime business partner, strongly criticized US-China tensions as "massively stupid" and urged reconciliation between the two nations. He also called for a ban on cryptocurrency, likening it to a "venereal disease" and deeming it "beneath contempt." Munger, a known bull on China, expressed his wish for better relations and predicted the continued strength of major tech companies like Apple, Google, and Microsoft.

feed.title: Google Creates $100 Million Fund for Skills Training Program (Published 2022)
feed.summary: Google has created a $100 million fund to support skills training and job placement for low-income Americans, aiming to help those without a four-year college degree find middle-class jobs. The initiative partners with non-profit groups like Year Up, Merit America, and Social Finance, with a unique financing model where students repay interest-free loans only if they secure jobs paying at least $40,000 annually. Google hopes this project will create a template for other companies and policymakers, ultimately fueling $1 billion in wage gains for 20,000 graduates.

feed.title: Pinterest General Counsel and Google Alumna Set to Step Down
feed.summary: Pinterest's General Counsel, Christine Flores, who was hired from Google in 2017, is set to step down on October 1. Flores will assist with the transition as the company searches for her replacement. She had previously sold off approximately $18 million in Pinterest stock over the past year.

feed.title: JPMorgan Chase, Toshiba and Ciena Build the First Quantum Key Distribution Network Used to Secure Mission-Critical Blockchain Application
feed.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Toshiba, and Ciena have successfully built and demonstrated the first quantum key distribution (QKD) network for metropolitan areas, securing a mission-critical blockchain application. This groundbreaking research proves the viability of QKD to detect and defend against potential quantum computing attacks, supporting 800 Gbps data rates under real-world conditions. The network secured Liink by J.P. Morgan, the world's first bank-led, production-grade, peer-to-peer blockchain network, showcasing the technology's effectiveness against future quantum threats.

feed.title: Walmart posts record holiday sales as spending remains firm
feed.summary: Walmart Inc. reported record holiday season sales, exceeding $150 billion in fourth-quarter revenue for the first time, defying supply chain issues and rising inflation. The company attributed its success to investments in chartering ships, raising worker wages, and sourcing over two-thirds of its products domestically, which helped it maintain competitive pricing, especially in groceries. Walmart forecasts continued sales and earnings gains for 2022, signaling confidence in sustained consumer spending.

feed.title: Kraft Heinz Invests In Consumer Insights With Kraft-O-Matic Data Platform
feed.summary: Kraft Heinz is enhancing its consumer insights capabilities by launching a new data platform called Kraft-O-Matic, in partnership with Google Cloud. This initiative leverages AI and machine learning to generate real-time data for product innovation and personalized consumer experiences, supporting Kraft Heinz's broader transformation strategy initiated in 2020. The company aims to improve speed to market, optimize its e-commerce marketing, and strengthen retail partnerships through these data-driven efforts.

feed.title: Salesforce ties executive compensation to ESG goals
feed.summary: Salesforce announced that a portion of executive variable pay for those at the executive vice president level and above will be tied to ESG measures, starting this fiscal year. These measures will focus on increasing representation for diverse employees and reducing air travel emissions, as well as increasing spend with suppliers signed onto Salesforce's Sustainability Exhibit. This move reflects a growing trend among major companies to link executive compensation to diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) and sustainability goals.

feed.title: Kraft Heinz Names Miguel Patricio as Chair Following Alex Behring's Retirement and James Park's Election to Board of Directors; Greg Abel Comments
feed.summary: The Kraft Heinz Company announced leadership changes to its Board of Directors, with CEO Miguel Patricio slated to become the new Chair following Alex Behring's retirement. Additionally, technology entrepreneur James Park will be nominated for election to the Board. These changes aim to continue strong leadership and integrate technology expertise into the company's strategy.

feed.title: Trump's new social media application 'Truth Social' begins gradual rollout
feed.summary: Donald Trump's "Truth Social" app began a gradual rollout on Sunday, with the aim of being fully operational in the US by the end of March. The platform is intended as an alternative to major social media sites that banned Trump after the January 6, 2021 Capitol assault. Former congressman Devin Nunes, CEO of Trump Media & Technology Group, stated that the app would be available on the Apple App Store, celebrating the return of free speech for those who felt their voices were canceled.

feed.title: Kraft Heinz taps Google for multiyear transformation push
feed.summary: Kraft Heinz announced a multiyear strategic partnership with Google to accelerate its digital transformation, leveraging Google Cloud's AI and ML to drive food innovations, build a customer data platform, and improve media efficiency. This initiative is part of Kraft Heinz's broader strategy to reinvest in its brands and achieve cost savings by 2024, enabling data-driven decisions as consumer behavior shifts online. The partnership aims to enhance personalization at scale, optimize media activations, and address changing market challenges amid the pandemic.

feed.title: LG AI Research forms 'Hyperscale' AI alliance with 13 companies
feed.summary: LG AI Research has formed an alliance with 13 companies and organizations to expand the use of its hyperscale AI engine, Exaone. The alliance aims to apply Exaone's capabilities, which include 300 billion parameters and multi-modal functions, across various sectors like IT, finance, and medical fields. Members will benefit from technologies such as Exaone Tuning, API access, and Exaone Playground, while contributing to the AI's further development and adoption.
