feed.title: Travelers Acquires Tech Assets of Insurtech Trōv for Personal Insurance
feed.summary: Travelers has acquired the technology assets of insurtech Trōv, an early innovator in micro-duration and embedded insurance. The deal, whose financial terms were not disclosed, will see Trōv's team and technology integrated into Travelers' Personal Insurance segment. This acquisition aligns with Travelers' ongoing strategy of investing over a billion dollars annually in technology to enhance customer, agent, and partner experiences.

feed.title: Vodafone announces circular economy plan
feed.summary: Vodafone has unveiled a comprehensive circular economy initiative focused on extending the life of mobile phones, encouraging trade-ins, and responsible recycling to minimize waste and reduce carbon emissions. The plan includes offering insurance, repair services, and a digital platform for easy trade-ins, alongside selling refurbished smartphones. This effort also involves expanding existing refurbishment programs for fixed-line equipment and committing to reuse or recycle 100% of network waste by 2025, alongside broader carbon reduction goals.

feed.title: Exclusive: Singapore flags concern to India over ban on Sea's game -sources
feed.summary: Singapore has expressed concerns to India regarding its ban on the popular gaming app "Free Fire," owned by Sea Ltd, marking the first diplomatic intervention since the ban. The move significantly impacted Sea's market value, and investors are worried about potential extensions to Sea's e-commerce app, Shopee. India had banned the app among others, citing data transfer to Chinese servers, a claim Sea refutes, stating it is a Singaporean company compliant with Indian law.

feed.title: Snowflake and Databricks back $222M round for dbt Labs at $4.2B valuation
feed.summary: dbt Labs, a fast-growing data management startup, has secured $222 million in funding, valuing the company at $4.2 billion. Notable investors in this round include Snowflake, Databricks, Alphabet’s GV fund, and Salesforce. The company plans to use the capital to hire 300 new employees over the next year and expand its offering as a popular data transformation tool used by over 25,000 data scientists and 9,000 companies.

feed.title: CRM giant Salesforce acquiring B.C.’s Traction on Demand
feed.summary: Salesforce.com Inc. is acquiring B.C.-based software firm Traction on Demand, which specializes in implementing marketing strategies using Salesforce's CRM services. The Burnaby-based company employs about 500 workers across British Columbia, and its founder had previously resisted selling the company. This acquisition follows Salesforce's recent spree of purchases, including Mobify and Slack Technologies Inc.

feed.title: Qualcomm Inc. stock rises Friday, still underperforms market
feed.summary: Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) stock rose 1.76% on Friday, closing at $170.93, despite underperforming the broader market. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average both saw larger gains. Qualcomm's stock remains below its 52-week high and showed mixed performance compared to competitors like Alphabet Inc. Cl A, NVIDIA Corp., and Cisco Systems Inc.

feed.title: WPP's Mark Read on why Coca-Cola, Google and Unilever are pivotal to the network's future
feed.summary: Mark Read, CEO of WPP, discussed the company's strong 2021 performance, driven by growth in digital marketing, media, e-commerce, data, and technology. He highlighted the importance of strategic partnerships with major clients like Coca-Cola, Google, and Unilever for future growth and client-agency collaboration. Read also addressed WPP's response to the situation in Ukraine, its hiring plans, and adjustments to workplace strategy.

feed.title: KYNDRYL REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FULL-YEAR 2021 RESULTS
feed.summary: Kyndryl Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: KD) reported its fourth-quarter and full-year 2021 financial results, with full-year revenues totaling $18.7 billion and a net loss of $2.3 billion. The company is strategically positioning itself for growth through new partnerships with cloud hyperscalers and key initiatives focused on increasing signings, transforming service delivery, and addressing substandard margins. Kyndryl also announced significant strategic partnerships with major cloud providers and an expanded customer base following its spin-off from IBM.

feed.title: How Does Google Make Money?
feed.summary: This article explains how Google, now Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL), generates revenue primarily through advertising on its search engine and web tools, as well as through its Google Cloud services and its "Other Bets" segment for new technologies. It details the financial performance of these segments and discusses Google's stock, leadership, and future plans including a stock split and AI expansion.

feed.title: Google, Meta face penalties in Russia as deadline passes to open local offices
feed.summary: Google and Meta are among several internet companies facing potential penalties in Russia for failing to establish local offices and comply with a new communications law. Russia's state communications regulator, Roskomnadzor, had set a deadline of the end of February for these companies to open local offices or face restrictions. The move is part of Russia's broader effort to control internet content, with fines previously issued for failing to censor anti-government content, and recent curtailments of access to platforms like Facebook in retaliation for censoring state media.

feed.title: At Snap Inc., Making Augmented Reality Work for Fashion
feed.summary: Snap Inc. is making significant strides in augmented reality (AR) for the fashion industry, with over 200 million Snapchat users engaging with AR daily. Peter Sellis, VP of Product at Snap Inc., discusses how AR technologies, including virtual try-ons and spatial technology, are evolving to enhance shopping experiences, reduce returns, and increase conversions for brands like Prada, Farfetch, and Gucci. The commercial benefits and future product innovations, such as cloth simulation and 3D asset management, are highlighted as key drivers for investment in AR within fashion.

feed.title: AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, TSMC and others join Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) group
feed.summary: Leading semiconductor companies including AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, Meta, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung, and TSMC have formed the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) industry consortium. This group aims to establish an open chiplet ecosystem by standardizing die-to-die interconnects, with the UCIe 1.0 specification already ratified. This initiative leverages existing PCI Express and Compute Express Link standards to enable easier mixing and matching of chiplet components from multiple vendors for System-on-Chip (SoC) construction.

feed.title: Check Point releases 2022 Cloud Security Report
feed.summary: Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. has released its 2022 Cloud Security Report, highlighting the challenges organizations face in securing cloud infrastructures amidst increasing cloud adoption, a cyber-skills shortage, and a rise in cloud security incidents, primarily due to misconfigurations. The report suggests a growing preference for independent cloud security solutions over cloud vendor security to streamline management across multi-cloud environments. TJ Gonen, VP of Cloud Security at Check Point, emphasizes the need for integrated third-party solutions with unified dashboards to simplify cloud security, reduce misconfiguration risks, and support application development in the cloud.

feed.title: Leveraging Technology to Improve The Lives of P&G Consumers
feed.summary: P&G utilizes advanced data-processing technologies like machine learning and artificial intelligence to enhance its products, understand consumer behavior, and streamline operations. This technology-driven approach, which began over five years ago, impacts everything from product development and quality control to personalized consumer communication and supply chain logistics. P&G's strategy focuses on connecting data, facilitating data scientists' work, and developing talent to continuously improve products and consumer experiences.

feed.title: Tripadvisor, Google Maps Suspend Reviews of Some Russian Listings
feed.summary: Google Maps and Tripadvisor have temporarily suspended new user reviews for certain listings in Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus. This action was taken in response to a flood of political statements posted as reviews, driven by a social media campaign urging activists to communicate with Russians via these platforms about the war in Ukraine. The companies aim to prevent the publishing of off-topic and abusive content.

feed.title: EA, Oracle Among Companies Heeding Ukraine Plea to Stop Business in Russia
feed.summary: Ukraine has requested that approximately 50 tech companies, including Oracle and EA, cease operations in Russia to isolate the country and pressure its government following military action. In response, Oracle announced the suspension of all operations in the Russian Federation, and EA Sports committed to removing Russian national and club teams from its FIFA games. Other major companies like Spotify, Twitter, Meta, Microsoft, and Google have also taken steps to restrict Russian state media or suspend services in Russia.

feed.title: Spotify closes its office in Russia in response to attack on Ukraine
feed.summary: Spotify announced the indefinite closure of its office in Russia in response to the country's attack on Ukraine. The music streaming platform stated its priority is its employees' safety and ensuring access to information. Spotify has also restricted the discoverability of Russian state-affiliated media and removed content from RT and Sputnik in several markets, while matching employee donations for humanitarian aid.

feed.title: DigitalOcean vs Cloudflare — which stock can take advantage of cloud expansion?
feed.summary: This article compares DigitalOcean Holdings (DOCN) and Cloudflare (NET), two cloud computing companies, to determine which is the better investment. DigitalOcean serves developers and SMBs, while Cloudflare focuses on web security and content delivery. The analysis concludes that Cloudflare is the less risky and better investment due to its continued large client growth and potential for SMB expansion, despite DigitalOcean's strong performance and hold in the SMB market.

feed.title: How Hyperscale Data Centers are reshaping India’s IT
feed.summary: Hyperscale data centers are critical infrastructure for companies like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, providing dedicated computing resources to handle massive user demands. These facilities are essential for the digital economy, supporting everything from emails to online shopping, and their importance has grown with trends like remote work and emerging technologies such as AI and IoT. India is poised for significant growth in its data center industry, driven by government incentives and an increasing need for robust data storage and processing capabilities, despite environmental concerns related to energy consumption.

feed.title: Sonos Roam SL vs Sonos Roam: which Bluetooth speaker will be the best?
feed.summary: This article compares the Sonos Roam SL and the Sonos Roam, two portable Bluetooth speakers from Sonos, to help consumers decide which one best suits their needs. The key difference lies in the Roam having a built-in microphone for voice controls, Auto Trueplay, and Sound Swap, features absent from the more affordable Roam SL. Both speakers share the same design, battery life, and core audio technology, making the choice dependent on budget and the importance of smart features.

feed.title: Kraft Heinz Partners With Google; Sanjiv Gajiwala and Giusy Buonfantino Detail
feed.summary: Kraft Heinz has formed a multi-year partnership with Google to leverage Google Cloud's data and analytics technologies, enhancing its marketing strategy and digital transformation. This collaboration aims to deepen consumer understanding, foster personalized engagement, and accelerate product innovation through data-driven insights. Key figures Sanjiv Gajiwala (Kraft Heinz) and Giusy Buonfantino (Google Solutions) emphasized the strategic importance of this alliance for future growth and consumer connection.

feed.title: Cloud management provider Cloocus receives $41 mn in Series B funding
feed.summary: Cloud management service provider Cloocus Co. has secured $40.8 million (50 billion won) in Series B funding from SK Inc. C&C as part of a larger 100 billion won round. This investment follows significant funding rounds for other Korean cloud MSPs like Megazone Cloud and Bespin Global. The capital injections reflect a turnaround for Korean MSPs, driven by increased demand for cloud services due to the pandemic and the growing adoption of SaaS and multicloud strategies.

feed.title: Primeprint Solution by Dentsply Sirona: The Medical-grade 3D Printing System for Dental Practices and Labs
feed.summary: Dentsply Sirona has launched the Primeprint Solution, an automated, end-to-end, medical-grade 3D printing system designed for dental practices and labs. This system aims to simplify and enhance the manufacturing of patient-specific and biocompatible dental appliances through DLP technology and automated post-processing. It integrates with Dentsply Sirona's digital ecosystem, developed in collaboration with Google Cloud, to offer a seamless and efficient workflow, maximizing productivity and ensuring high-quality, regulated results.

feed.title: Cloudflare and Akamai to continue operations in Russia
feed.summary: Cloudflare and Akamai have stated their intention to continue operations in Russia despite calls to cease business following the invasion of Ukraine. Both companies argue that providing internet access is crucial for Russian citizens to obtain accurate information, rather than contributing to an information blackout. They have, however, condemned the invasion and ceased business with sanctioned entities or state-majority-owned customers.

feed.title: Cisco Stops Business In Russia, Ups Security Efforts In Ukraine
feed.summary: Cisco Systems has halted all business operations in Russia and Belarus in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The company is also providing security assistance to Ukraine through its Talos threat intelligence team, offering free software auto-renewals, Webex meetings, and calls to the country. This move aligns Cisco with other major tech companies sanctioning Russia, and the company has also established a humanitarian fund for Ukraine.

feed.title: Super-app, moomoo, is the only investment platform to break through top five most downloaded finance apps in Singapore in 2021 since its launch - PR Newswire APAC
feed.summary: Moomoo, an investment super-app, has become the only investment platform to rank among the top five most downloaded finance apps in Singapore's Apple App Store and Google Play Store in 2021 since its launch on March 8, 2021. The platform, a subsidiary of Nasdaq-listed Futu Holdings, also announced its official debut in Australia on March 8, 2022. Moomoo has rapidly expanded in Singapore, acquiring 220,000 registered users and 100,000 paying clients within its first three months, and has obtained approvals-in-principle for all SGX memberships, aiming to be a full-service digital investment platform.

feed.title: Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Stock Price Has Fallen 12.8% in 2022. Should You Buy It?
feed.summary: Alphabet's stock (GOOGL) has dropped 12.8% in 2022, leading many to question if it's a good buying opportunity. Despite plateauing ad revenues, Google is expanding into cloud services and cybersecurity, highlighted by its acquisition of Mandiant. The company is considered attractive at current prices, though antitrust concerns remain a risk.

feed.title: Our Ultimate Stock-Pickers' Top 10 Buys and Sells
feed.summary: This article identifies the top 10 high-conviction buys and sells among Morningstar's Ultimate Stock-Pickers for the fourth quarter of 2021, based on an aggregate analysis of their holdings. It highlights key companies like Microsoft and 3M as top buys and Marsh & McLennan as a prominent sell, detailing the Morningstar analysts' fair value estimates, economic moats, and investment theses for these firms. The report assists investors by providing insights into attractive investment ideas and valuation considerations.

feed.title: Amazon announces 20-for-1 stock split, $10 bln share buyback
feed.summary: Amazon.com Inc. has announced a 20-for-1 stock split and authorized a $10 billion share buyback plan, causing its shares to rise by 7% in extended trading. This marks Amazon's first stock split since 1999, aimed at making shares more accessible to investors and increasing flexibility for employees managing equity. Trading with the new share price will commence on June 6.

feed.title: CrowdStrike’s Crowd-Pleaser; Build-A-Bear’s Blunder; Asana’s Attitude Adjustment
feed.summary: This article discusses the financial performance and market outlook for several companies. CrowdStrike reported impressive earnings and strong guidance, positioning it well in the growing cybersecurity market. Build-A-Bear Workshop issued a cautious 2022 outlook due to inflation, leading to investor concern, while Amazon announced a 20-for-1 stock split, mirroring Alphabet's earlier move. Additionally, Asana reported significant losses despite revenue growth, and PayPal faced a downgrade from BofA Securities due to concerns about the Russia-Ukraine conflict's impact.

feed.title: Amazon announces 20-for-1 stock split
feed.summary: Amazon announced a 20-for-1 stock split, following similar moves by other major tech companies like Alphabet, Apple, and Tesla. The article explains that a stock split divides existing shares into multiple, smaller-priced shares without changing the overall value of an investor's holdings or the company's market capitalization. Stock splits are often done to increase a stock's liquidity and make it more accessible to a wider range of investors, though in an era of fractional shares, some of the practical impact is diminished.

feed.title: Amazon surges as stock split, buyback excite investors
feed.summary: Amazon's stock surged over 5% after the company announced a 20-for-1 stock split and a $10 billion share buyback, aiming to attract more investors and boost confidence. This move follows a period of lackluster performance for the e-commerce giant, despite its substantial growth since its IPO. The stock split, the first since 1999, and the buyback are seen as psychological boosts and a signal that management views the stock as undervalued.

feed.title: Grizzle Growth ETF (GRZZ) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
feed.summary: This article provides detailed information on the Grizzle Growth ETF (GRZZ), including its current stock price, historical data, and performance metrics. It outlines the ETF's investment strategy, top holdings like NVIDIA and Microsoft, and sector weightings. The page also features related ETF news and research reports from analysts regarding other companies.

feed.title: Russia says it will block Instagram
feed.summary: Russia announced it would block Instagram, blaming a recent change in Meta's hate-speech policy that temporarily allowed some users to call for violence against Russians in the context of the Ukraine war. This move is part of Russia's broader effort to control information flow and prevent its citizens from accessing uncensored news about the invasion. The ban is expected to affect 80 million Russian users.

feed.title: ‘The Dirty Dozen List’ – Corporations Enable and Profit from Sexual Exploitation
feed.summary: The National Center on Sexual Exploitation (NCOSE) has released its annual "Dirty Dozen List," highlighting twelve mainstream entities accused of facilitating and profiting from sexual abuse and exploitation. The list includes technology giants like Google, Meta, Discord, and others, pointing to various ways they enable access to harmful content or profit from commercial sex industries. NCOSE details specific examples for each company and offers ways for the public to take action against these practices.

feed.title: 5 Artificial Intelligence Growth Stocks to Buy Now and Hold
feed.summary: The artificial intelligence (AI) industry is projected to grow significantly, from an estimated $93 billion in 2021 to $997 billion annually by 2028. This article highlights five AI growth stocks—C3.ai, Upstart, Splunk, Alphabet, and Lemonade—that are positioned to capitalize on this expansion by leveraging AI in various sectors, from enterprise solutions and lending to data analysis and insurance, offering investors opportunities for long-term growth.

feed.title: Instacart Unveils Shoppable Recipes, New Product Integrations With TikTok, Tasty, Hearst Magazines And More
feed.summary: Instacart has launched "Shoppable Recipes," a new feature that allows users to seamlessly purchase ingredients for recipes found on platforms like TikTok and Hearst Magazines' food properties (e.g., Delish). This initiative aims to transform online recipe browsing into immediate action, providing a new avenue for food creators to monetize content and for Instacart's retail partners to reach new customers. The integration leverages Instacart's extensive grocery catalog and AI to enable quick delivery of in-stock items.

feed.title: Musk’s Starlink Brings Internet to Ukraine, and Attention to a New Space Race
feed.summary: Elon Musk's Starlink has provided crucial satellite broadband service to Ukraine, particularly as Russian forces target infrastructure. This assistance highlights the growing importance of low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, championed by companies like SpaceX and Amazon, in a new space race for global internet connectivity. These LEO satellites offer a smaller, more affordable alternative to traditional geostationary satellites for delivering internet access.

feed.title: Why banks and NATO are worrying about a future ‘Quantum attack’
feed.summary: The article discusses the growing concern among banks and organizations like NATO about the potential for "quantum attacks" as quantum computing technology advances. Andersen Cheng, CEO of Post Quantum, warns that powerful quantum computers capable of cracking current encryption methods may be closer than initially thought, posing a significant threat to critical communications, financial data, and cryptocurrencies. The piece highlights how various nations are investing heavily in quantum technology and the commercial sector is beginning to prepare for this shift.

feed.title: Berkshire Hathaway shares topped $500,000 each—here's why Warren Buffett says he'll never split the stock
feed.summary: Class A shares of Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway recently closed above $500,000 each for the first time, making it the sixth most valuable company in the U.S. Despite calls for a stock split to lower share prices, Buffett has consistently refused, arguing that the high price attracts sophisticated, long-term investors. He believes a split would lead to a less aligned shareholder base and offers no intrinsic value if not tied to company growth.

feed.title: MSG Entertainment Names Lucas Watson President, MSG Sphere
feed.summary: Madison Square Garden Entertainment Corp. announced the appointment of Lucas Watson as President, MSG Sphere, effective March 28. In this role, Watson will lead the business strategy and execution for MSG Sphere, the company's planned immersive entertainment venues, including go-to-market planning and bookings. The first MSG Sphere venue is scheduled to open in Las Vegas in the second half of 2023, and Watson will also oversee the global development of the MSG Sphere brand.

feed.title: Lawsuit Accuses Google of Bias Against Black Employees (Published 2022)
feed.summary: A former Google employee, April Curley, has filed a class-action lawsuit against the company, alleging systematic discrimination against Black workers. The lawsuit claims Google places Black employees in lower-level jobs, underpays them, and denies them opportunities for advancement, echoing longstanding complaints about the company's diversity issues. Google's 2021 diversity report showed Black employees make up 4.4% of its U.S. workforce, which is below the national average for digital publishing and search companies.

feed.title: GM bets $3.5 billion more on self-driving tech unit as SoftBank exits
feed.summary: General Motors (GM) is increasing its investment in its self-driving car subsidiary, Cruise, by approximately $3.5 billion, as SoftBank's Vision Fund exits its stake. GM will pay $2.1 billion to acquire SoftBank's share and make another $1.35 billion investment committed by SoftBank in 2018, bringing GM's total stake to 80%. This move raises questions about Cruise's near-term revenue generation and the financial commitment required from GM and its partners to fund the unit's development.

feed.title: Racism at Google? Alphabet Inc's Google discriminates against Black people, former staffer claims
feed.summary: A former Google employee, April Curley, has filed a lawsuit alleging that Alphabet Inc.'s Google discriminates against Black people by pigeon-holing them into low-paying, dead-end jobs and subjecting them to harassment. Curley, who was fired in 2020 after advocating for reform regarding the treatment of Black employees, claims that Google's leadership lacks Black representation, leading to biased hiring practices and limited advancement opportunities for Black professionals. The lawsuit highlights Google's slow progress in diversifying its workforce and its struggles in retaining Black employees, despite efforts to increase hiring after 2020.

feed.title: Jury: Employer’s DEI training didn’t conflict with worker’s religious beliefs
feed.summary: A federal jury ruled that a born-again Christian employee's religious beliefs did not conflict with his employer's mandatory Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) training. The employee, who was later fired, had refused to complete a course question about identifying harassment of a transgender co-worker, claiming a conflict with his beliefs. The jury found that while he had sincerely held beliefs, they did not conflict with the company's employment requirement, highlighting the employer's appropriate response of focusing on workplace behavior rather than personal beliefs.

feed.title: Google’s revamped Contact Center AI Platform provides tighter integration with CRMs
feed.summary: Google Cloud has updated its Contact Center AI Platform to offer a comprehensive, out-of-the-box solution with tighter integration with popular CRM software. This aims to provide businesses with cloud scalability, unified data across sales, marketing, and support, and more personalized customer experiences. The platform also expands its partnership with Salesforce.com Inc. to integrate with Service Cloud Voice.

feed.title: The BlackBerry veteran who took on Google and won
feed.summary: Patrick Spence, CEO of Sonos, a veteran of BlackBerry (formerly Research In Motion), successfully led Sonos in a patent infringement lawsuit against Google. The U.S. International Trade Commission ruled in favor of Sonos, affirming that Google infringed on five of Sonos's patents related to smart speaker technology. This victory demonstrates that smaller companies can win intellectual property disputes against large tech giants, emboldening Sonos and potentially setting the stage for future actions against other major players like Amazon.

feed.title: Microsoft looks poised to dominate the quantum computing industry
feed.summary: Microsoft has recently announced a breakthrough in quantum computing with the invention of "topological qubits," which they claim will lead to scalable quantum computers. This development positions Microsoft to become a major player in the quantum industry, complementing their existing Azure quantum services and a new partnership with Pasqal for near-term 1,000-qubit processor access. While the ultimate winner in quantum computing is uncertain, Microsoft's comprehensive strategy, including both long-term qubit research and immediate cloud solutions, suggests it's a strong contender for a dominant market share.

feed.title: Alphabet spins off its Sandbox AQ quantum computing unit
feed.summary: Alphabet Inc.'s quantum computing unit, Sandbox AQ, has spun off into an independent company after raising a "nine-figure" funding round from prominent investors like Eric Schmidt and Marc Benioff. The new startup, led by CEO Jack Hidary, aims to develop commercially viable quantum technologies, focusing initially on post-quantum cryptography software and quantum simulation in healthcare and materials science. Sandbox AQ already has customers, including Mount Sinai Health System and SoftBank Group Corp.'s telecom business, and plans to work with multiple cloud providers, including Google Cloud.

feed.title: Independent Sandbox AQ Launches, Prominent Investors Including T. Rowe Price, Eric Schmidt, Breyer Capital, Guggenheim Partners and Thomas Tull, and Customers
feed.summary: Sandbox AQ, an enterprise SaaS company leveraging quantum tech and AI, officially launched with significant backing from prominent investors including T. Rowe Price, Eric Schmidt, Breyer Capital, Guggenheim Partners, and Thomas Tull. Eric Schmidt will serve as chairman of Sandbox AQ’s board of directors, and the company plans to hire additional AI experts, physicists, and engineers. Sandbox AQ is developing commercial products for various sectors, focusing on post-quantum cryptography, drug development, clean energy, and data security, and has already secured global customers like Vodafone Business and Mt. Sinai Health System.

feed.title: Towards The Distant Virtual World: Vitalii Vashchuk Shares Insights
feed.summary: Vitalii Vashchuk, Director and Gaming Technologist at EPAM Systems, shared his insights on the metaverse's evolution and the underlying technologies. He describes the metaverse as a concept aimed at enhancing communication and experiences, offering greater freedom than Web2.0. Key technologies enabling the metaverse include Blockchain, NFTs, AI, and IoT.

feed.title: Mizuho plans to tie up with Google to serve clients better
feed.summary: Mizuho Financial Group Inc. announced a strategic alliance with Google to enhance its client services. The Japanese financial firm aims to use Google's expertise to analyze client transaction data for improved customer service quality and to offer other financial services through the Google Cloud platform.

feed.title: WT Dining Services Launches Mobile Ordering
feed.summary: WT Dining Services, in partnership with Aramark, has launched mobile ordering for Chick-fil-A, Which Wich, and Pony Express Burritos at West Texas A&M University. The new service, available through the Transact Mobile Ordering App, allows students, faculty, staff, and community members to order and pay using various methods, including Dining Dollars, Buff Cash, and credit/debit cards. This initiative aims to enhance customer service by providing a convenient way to access menu items.

feed.title: Kroger partners with Nvidia to boost freshness efforts using AI
feed.summary: Kroger has announced a strategic collaboration with Nvidia to enhance its fresh food initiatives using artificial intelligence and online simulations. The partnership will establish a lab and demonstration center at Kroger's headquarters to develop AI-driven methods for identifying food spoilage, optimizing delivery routes, and improving in-store efficiency. This move aims to leverage technology to extend the shelf life of fresh produce and improve customer service, aligning with Kroger's "Fresh for Everyone" branding.

feed.title: Netflix buys another video game studio as it builds out its gaming business. (Published 2022)
feed.summary: Netflix announced it acquired Boss Fight Entertainment, a mobile game developer, marking its third studio purchase as it expands into the video game market. This move is part of Netflix's strategy to differentiate itself by leveraging popular shows for game development and eventually creating original games, aiming for a careful expansion after seeing other tech companies struggle in the gaming industry.

feed.title: Perfect Corp.’s YouCam Apps Reach over 1 Billion Downloads Worldwide
feed.summary: Perfect Corp.'s YouCam Suite of Apps has achieved "Super App" status, surpassing 1 billion global app downloads. The suite, which includes YouCam Makeup, YouCam Perfect, YouCam Video, and YouCam Nail, leverages AI and AR technologies for beauty, photo effects, and video editing, generating 1.68 billion virtual try-ons monthly. The company attributes its success to best-in-class AI and AR innovations, fostering a loyal community that spends over 530 million minutes monthly within the YouCam universe.

feed.title: Brookfield agrees to buy Hibernia REIT for $1.2 billion
feed.summary: Brookfield Asset Management Inc. has reached an agreement to acquire Hibernia REIT Plc for approximately 1.09 billion euros ($1.2 billion) in cash, causing Hibernia's shares to surge to a record high. The deal, which offers a 33.9% premium over Hibernia's average share price, sees Brookfield expanding its real estate portfolio in Dublin, a market where tech giants are rapidly growing. Brookfield is actively investing in European office landlords, capitalizing on market uncertainty and discounts to asset values.

feed.title: Toyota, Aurora Test-Drive Autonomous Ride-Hailing Fleet In Texas
feed.summary: Toyota and Aurora Innovation Inc. have begun testing an autonomous ride-hailing fleet in Texas using Toyota's Sienna minivans equipped with Aurora's self-driving system. The tests, conducted with two safety operators and no passengers, will cover highways and suburban streets in the Dallas-Fort-Worth area, including routes to the airport. This initiative aims to generate revenue from significant engineering investments in autonomous vehicle technology and prepares for a commercial launch on ride-hailing networks like Uber.

feed.title: CEO interview: Silicon Labs’ Matt Johnson on balancing breadth and focus
feed.summary: Matt Johnson, CEO of Silicon Labs, discusses the company's strategic shift to focus entirely on the IoT market after divesting its infrastructure and automotive businesses. He highlights the importance of offering complete, application- and software-led solutions for diverse wireless technologies in IoT, emphasizing security and continuous integration for cost, performance, and power reduction. Johnson also touches on the company's approach to manufacturing and capital deployment, including M&A and share repurchases.

feed.title: KKR Values Behavioral-Health Startup Brightline at $705 Million
feed.summary: Behavioral-health startup Brightline announced a valuation of $705 million after securing $105 million in a funding round led by KKR & Co. Existing investors, including Alphabet Inc.'s venture arm GV and Optum Ventures, also participated in the funding. Brightline provides virtual behavioral-health services to children and their families.

feed.title: Best Global Company Culture 2022
feed.summary: Comparably’s annual Best Global Company Culture list for 2022 ranks the top large companies (over 500 employees) with international operations based on anonymous employee feedback collected over the past year. The list highlights companies with strong cultures across nearly 20 categories, including compensation, leadership, and work-life balance, making it a relevant resource for job seekers worldwide. Microsoft, IBM, and Google took the top three spots, respectively, among the 50 recognized global companies.

feed.title: Google Play Store App practices: France slaps $2 mn penalty on Google
feed.summary: The Paris Commercial Court has fined Google 2 million euros ($2.2 million) for abusive practices against developers on its Play Store. Google is also required to amend seven clauses from its contracts from 2015 and 2016, which included a 30% commission on developer revenues. The French Ministry of Finance initiated the legal action in 2018, citing a significant imbalance in rights and obligations for app developers.

feed.title: IonQ Named As One Of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies
feed.summary: IonQ (NYSE: IONQ), a leader in trapped-ion quantum computing, has been recognized on TIME’s annual TIME100 Most Influential Companies list for its leadership in commercializing quantum computing. The company was included in the "New Frontiers" category, acknowledging its extraordinary impact and recent achievements, including the introduction of IonQ Aria, the world's most powerful quantum computer. This recognition follows a year of significant business momentum and technical breakthroughs for IonQ.

feed.title: DoubleLine Shiller CAPE US Equities ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:DCPE)
feed.summary: The DoubleLine Shiller CAPE US Equities ETF (NYSEARCA:DCPE) was launched on March 31, 2022, and is an actively managed ETF aiming to outperform the S&P 500 Index by investing in undervalued US stocks chosen based on the CAPE ratio and momentum factors. As of May 2026, its stock was trading at $32.46 with assets under management of $33.11 million and a net expense ratio of 0.65%. The ETF's top holdings include Meta Platforms, Linde, and Alphabet.

feed.title: GameStop Soars on Plans to Extend Rebound With Stock Split
feed.summary: GameStop (GME) shares soared by as much as 22% in extended trading following the announcement of plans to propose a stock split to shareholders in the form of a dividend. The company intends to ask for approval to increase its Class A shares from 300 million to 1 billion at its upcoming annual meeting. This move led to a significant jump in the stock price, reaching $203.98 after closing at $166.58.
